links.outcome: LLM treatment recommendation quality (mSCS) versus real multidisciplinary tumor boards, noninferiority margin 0.15
links.effect: MTB mean mSCS 0.849; Claude 3.5 Sonnet 0.731 (95% CI 0.697-0.765) narrowly missed noninferiority margin of 0.699; ChatGPT-4 0.660 (95% CI 0.623-0.696) clearly below.
links.quote: The mean mSCS score of the MTBs was 0.849 (standard deviation [SD] = 0.157), setting the noninferiority margin at 0.699.

links.outcome: LLM performance on intended-use oncology decision support with real-world-like case scenarios
links.effect: Neither LLM matched tumor board standards; Claude 0.731 and ChatGPT-4 0.660 versus MTB 0.849; better performance in locally advanced than metastatic cases (p < 0.05).
links.quote: Neither LLM matched the MTB standards.

screen.reason: Empirical noninferiority evaluation of ChatGPT-4 and Claude 3.5 Sonnet against multidisciplinary tumor boards across 110 representative genitourinary cancer case scenarios rated by blinded oncologists. It tests model performance rather than a specific deployment guardrail or organizational practice.
